findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() panics on file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted path or missing file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error type); propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect inside a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: pure-looking core function has observable side effects; breaks functional-core/imperative-shell separation and makes the function non-deterministic with respect to stdout
findings.fix: remove println!; if logging is required, pass a logger trait or return parsed data only; shell layer handles logging

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() — collects all split parts into Vec when only two fields exist; should use split_once for first-delimiter extraction
findings.failure_mode: allocates intermediate Vec of all parts, wastes heap memory, and silently ignores lines with more or fewer commas instead of reporting them
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(MissingDelimiter) to get (name_part, value_part) directly with one allocation

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with no comma triggers index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime
findings.fix: use split_once and match on the Some/None result; if using split, use parts.get(0).ok_or(MissingField("name"))

findings.failure_mode: same as line 16; missing delimiter causes panic instead of typed error
findings.fix: use split_once; bind name from the first tuple element directly without indexing

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on parse panics on non-numeric input; also uses unchecked indexing for parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: any non-numeric second field crashes the program; missing second field also crashes via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(MissingField("value"))?.trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(ParseError)? — parse directly to u16 to avoid lossy cast, propagate errors

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as cast after parse; value > 65535 silently truncates
findings.failure_mode: input value 70000 parses to u32 70000 then truncates to u16 4464 — data corruption without any error or warning
findings.fix: parse directly to u16 via .parse::<u16>() to let the parser reject out-of-range values, or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(OverflowError)?

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic and returns Vec directly instead of Result
findings.failure_mode: no error path at all — every failure mode (missing file, read error, malformed line, parse error, index out of bounds) manifests as panic rather than typed error; functional-core/imperative-shell boundary is violated
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> that handles I/O; (2) pure fn parse_sessions(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that does parsing; both return Result

findings.problem: println! in the middle of a map closure — side effect inside iterator pipeline
findings.failure_mode: breaks referential transparency; the function has hidden observable behavior; makes testing and reasoning about purity impossible
findings.fix: remove println! from the parser; if logging is needed, apply it in the shell layer after parse_sessions returns

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for load_sessions — no baseline measurement for I/O or parsing performance
findings.failure_mode: no evidence to validate whether parsing is acceptable, whether allocation patterns are optimal, or whether changes regress performance
findings.fix: add benches/ directory with criterion or similar benchmark for load_sessions and parse_sessions

no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in load_sessions

no second-ring evidence for release behavior or assembly

I/O in core, unchecked indexing via parts[] instead of split_once/get, lossy as cast truncating u32 to u16, and mixed I/O/parsing without Result return types.
